results.note: IMSLP: 2 clarinets, string quartet 'or strings', 35-40 min, manuscript-based, no date. Wikipedia: clarinets in B-flat and A with string quartet. Urania movements total 38.6 min (4 movements).
IMSLP: composed 1807/07/30, dedicated to Dauprat, db ad lib., 25-30 min, published 1827-28. Czech Nonet (Praga, 2008) 4 movements total 27 min.

IMSLP and the Le Concert de la Loge disc say nine solo instruments (oboe, clarinet, bassoon, horn, 2 vn, va, vc, db), D major, 4 movements, 34.6 min. Wikipedia's list adds a flute for No. 1 (ten players); the nine-player scoring follows the sources opened.
Huenteler et al. (Dabringhaus und Grimm 1996): No. 2 in A major has 4 movements incl. Adagio di molto and Minuetto, 21.3 min.
Op. 51 for flute, violin, cello on Rampal/Stern/Rostropovich (Sony 1990): variations 8.9 + fantasy 8.5 = 17.4 min; Wikipedia: Leipzig 1804.
Grand Trio for flute, violin, cello in G: 4 movements; MDG 1992 31.4 min, cpo 2024 35.0 min. Wikipedia: Vienna, before 1815.
Trio Domenica (Quintone 2022): F major, 4 movements incl. Fuga a due soggetti, 16.0 min. Wikipedia lists the trio.
Clarton CQ 0024-2 (1996) 'Quintetto in Es No. 1': 7 movements incl. Polonese and Andantino con variazzioni, 26.9 min; flute, clarinet, horn, viola, bassoon.
Clarton 'No. 2': 6 movements, Andante con variazioni and closing Rondeau, 32.7 min; cpo 2024 (Albert-Schweitzer-Ensemble) has the same work, 32.7 min.

Wikipedia: 'Unrevealed, Lord Byron to Augusta Leigh' for baritone and string quartet (1981). Cherubini Quartett with Fischer-Dieskau (Orfeo, rec. 1988/89) 37:47; Kreuzberger/Salter (CPO 2021) 39.9 min.
IMSLP: E-flat, 1853 first publication, 25 min, Gurlitt dedication. Linos Ensemble (cpo): 4 movements incl. Intermezzo, 25.7 min.

Linos Ensemble: 4 movements, 2nd Andante con variazioni, 28.6 min. Year 1866 is the Cranz print; Wikipedia says the Gewandhaus Quartet premiered it in 1865, so composition may be a year or so earlier.
Reinhold Quartett (cpo 2019, complete): 4 movements, 25.6 min, 'No. 1 in E-flat major, op. 16'. Wikipedia's work list dates Op. 16 to 1843 (year was blank).
Reinhold Quartett (cpo 2019): 'No. 5 in G minor, op. 287', 4 movements, 28.9 min; the last of five quartets. No date found.
IMSLP: 'Cello (or Violin), Harmonium and Piano', first printed 1892. Verdin et al. (VDE-GALLO 2019): 3 movements, 19.0 min.
VDE-GALLO 2019 (Joris Verdin et al., 'Reference Harmonium Vol. 5'): Trio No. 1 in F, Op. 28, 3 movements, 17.3 min. No IMSLP page found; no violin alternative confirmed.
VDE-GALLO 2019: Trio No. 2 in F minor, Op. 30, 4 movements, 25.0 min. No IMSLP page found.

fixes.notes: Dedicated to Madame Henriette Vogt (spelling per IMSLP); four movements

results.note: Hungaroton 32488 (Trio Art Nouveau): 4 movements, 35.6 min. IMSLP prints the dedicatee as 'Madame Henriette Vogt' (not Voigt); no source found identifying her with the Leipzig Henriette Voigt, so the note follows IMSLP. IMSLP date is '1833?', Silvertrust 'the 1830s'.

Hungaroton 32488: Op. 164 in G, 4 movements, 11.5+8.0+6.6+6.2 = 32.3 min (minutes was empty); Hungaroton numbers it No. 15, Deezer No. 24, so the title stays unnumbered. IMSLP: '1er Trio facile et brillant', 1842.

results.note: Wikipedia: 'Piano Quintet in D major, Op. 23 (1949)'; Continuum CCD 1024 lists 'Piano Quintet in D major, op.23' with the Melos Ensemble. 4 movements, 33.0 min. Key and opus were missing from the title.

IMSLP: Bb, c. 1901, pub. c. 1910, 25 min, 'Harp (or Piano)'. Harp recording found: Valerie Milot, Analekta 2017 (4 movements, 31.7 min); Trio Nuori (Ligia 2018, with piano) 26.8 min. Wikipedia also cites a harp recording (de Maistre, Turban, Yang).

Brodsky Quartet (Challenge Classics 2007): 4 movements (Allegro moderato, Tema con variazioni, Intermezzo, Finale), 29.4 min. Year 1907 on score and in Wikipedia's list (Pedarra: 1904); P. 53 is the Pedarra catalogue.
Da Vinci Ensemble (Brilliant Classics): Doppio Quartet in D minor, P.27, 4 movements incl. two Intermezzi, 20.8 min; ROctet also records it. Year left blank (no source found).

IMSLP's list says the R. numbers were 'invented by Nicholas Lewis (IMSLP Cataloging)', not a scholarly catalogue, so 'R. 14' comes out of the title. Work itself checks: 2 movements, 1930, Cuarteto Latinoamericano 10.6 min. The other Revueltas titles (R. 15, 16, 28, 34) have the same problem.

1921 Simrock quartet (Nimbus NI 5506 'No. 1 in C-sharp minor (1921)'; IMSLP 'No. 3'). Reznicek also wrote an earlier C-sharp minor quartet (1906, IMSLP 'No. 2', 5 movements, not in the catalogue). Both discs have 4 movements, 26-29 min.
IMSLP: String Quartet No. 5 in E minor, 1925-30, Gertig 81. Minguet Quartett (CPO 2020): 2 movements, 16.6 min.
IMSLP: B-flat, Forberg 1881, 30-35 min, Guillot de Sainbris dedication. Trio Parnassus: 4 movements incl. Romanze, 29.3 min; Goebel Trio 33.7 min.
